headings.title: Infractions not criminal offenses and no legal disability
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that an infraction is not a criminal offense and conviction creates no criminal-conviction disability or legal disadvantage.

headings.title: Misdemeanor procedure applicable to infractions
headings.reviewNote: Applies misdemeanor procedure to infractions except as otherwise provided by law.

headings.title: Default judgment for failure to appear or respond and motion to set aside
headings.reviewNote: Permits default judgment for fines and costs upon failure to appear or respond to section 476.385 central violations bureau notice absent good cause/excusable neglect, enforceable under sections 488.5028/488.5030 with first-class mail notice and six-month set-aside motion.

headings.title: Arrest warrant authority for infractions and chapter 307 exception
headings.reviewNote: Permits court to issue a warrant for failure to appear on an infraction notwithstanding subsection 3, except for infractions under chapter 307.

headings.title: Judgment amount limited to statutory fine and court costs
headings.reviewNote: Limits infraction judgment against defendant to the authorized fine and court costs for the offense.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 5 subsections and statutory history; revised subsection 4 title to reference chapter 307 directly and verified noncriminal infraction status, misdemeanor procedure, default judgments, and fine/cost limits.

headings.title: Application of criminal code to offenses committed after January 1, 1979
headings.reviewNote: Provides that criminal code provisions govern construction, punishment, and defenses for code offenses committed after January 1, 1979.

headings.title: Construction of non-code offenses committed after January 1, 1979
headings.reviewNote: Keeps unrepealed non-code offenses in effect while applying code construction and defense rules to those committed after January 1, 1979 unless otherwise provided or context requires.

headings.title: Inapplicability of criminal code to pre-1979 offenses
headings.reviewNote: Excludes offenses committed before January 1, 1979 from the code, requiring construction and punishment under prior law notwithstanding section 1.160.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 3 subsections, statutory history, and effective date 1-01-79; post-1979 code and non-code offense construction and pre-1979 exclusion notwithstanding section 1.160 verified.

headings.title: No statute of limitations for murder, class A felonies, and sex offenses
headings.reviewNote: Permits commencing prosecution at any time for murder, first-degree or forcible rape or sodomy (and attempts), or any class A felony.

headings.title: General statutes of limitations for felonies, misdemeanors, and infractions
headings.reviewNote: Sets default limitation periods at three years for felonies, one year for misdemeanors, six months for infractions, and five years for class B felony section 569.040 or section 569.050/569.055 violations.

headings.title: Extended limitations periods for fraud, official misconduct, and child support fraud
headings.reviewNote: Permits extended prosecutions (capped at three extra years) for fraud/fiduciary breach (including sections 407.511–407.556), public official misconduct, and willful fraudulent child support arrearage claims.

headings.title: Time of commission of offense and continuous course of conduct
headings.reviewNote: Defines offense commission as when every element occurs or continuing conduct terminates, with time starting the day after commission.

headings.title: Commencement of prosecution for felonies, misdemeanors, and infractions
headings.reviewNote: Defines prosecution commencement as information filing for misdemeanors or infractions and complaint or indictment filing for felonies.

headings.title: Tolling of limitations period for absence, concealment, pending cases, or DNA identification
headings.reviewNote: Tolls limitations during absence from state (max three-year extension), concealment, pending Missouri prosecution, section 552.020 mental unfitness, or period from published DNA profile report until named match.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 6 subsections, statutory history, and 2 case annotations (State v. Meeks, State v. Mixon); refined subsection 2 note to cite sections 569.040, 569.050, and 569.055 directly and verified limitations, extensions, commencement, and DNA/absence tolling.

headings.title: No time limitation for sexual offenses involving age eighteen or under
headings.reviewNote: Permits commencing prosecutions at any time notwithstanding section 556.036 for unlawful sexual offenses involving a person eighteen years of age or under (note catchline says 'under eighteen').

headings.title: Scope of sexual offenses including mandatory sex offender registry offenses
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that 'sexual offenses' includes all offenses requiring registration under sections 589.400 to 589.425 without limitation.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections, statutory history, and 2 cross-references (537.046, 516.371); revised subsection 1 title to reflect exact body scope ('eighteen years of age or under' vs catchline 'under eighteen').

headings.title: Conviction of included offenses and statutory definitions
headings.reviewNote: Permits conviction of an included offense defined by same/fewer facts, statutory lesser-degree denomination, or attempt.

headings.title: Rational basis requirement for jury charge on included offenses
headings.reviewNote: Provides court is not obligated to instruct on an included offense absent a rational basis to acquit of the charged offense and convict of the included offense, defining 'charged' offense.

headings.title: Mandatory instruction on requested included offense with rational basis
headings.reviewNote: Obligates court to instruct on a particular included offense only if requested and a rational evidentiary basis exists to acquit of the immediately higher included offense and convict of that offense.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 3 subsections, statutory history, and 2 case annotations (Wilkerson, Hill); included-offense definitions, rational-basis instruction rule, and requested-instruction duty for immediately higher included offenses verified.

headings.title: Lack of victim consent as element in restraint and kidnapping offenses
headings.reviewNote: Establishes lack of victim consent to confinement, movement, or restraint as an element of offenses under sections 565.110 to 565.130.

headings.title: Causes of lack of consent from forcible compulsion or incapacity
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that lack of consent results from forcible compulsion or incapacity to consent.

headings.title: Deemed incapacity to consent for persons under fourteen or incapacitated
headings.reviewNote: Deems a person incapable of consent if less than fourteen years of age or incapacitated.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 3 subsections, transfer note (formerly 565.100), and effective date 1-01-17; lack-of-consent element for sections 565.110 to 565.130, forcible compulsion/incapacity causes, and under-14/incapacitated deemed incapacity verified.
